newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits narrowly mixed before GDP.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits narrowly mixed before GDP.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were mixed on Wednesday in moderate trade, dealers said.

They said most traders were sidelined before today's issue of the first-quarter gross domestic product (GDP), which is forecast to show a 4.1 percent annual growth rate compared with 3.8 percent growth reported in the fourth-quarter 1996.

The American Production and Inventory Control (APICS) survey, New York National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM) index and Chicago Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) figures being released later on Wednesday will probably be overshadowed by the GDP numbers, dealers said.

"Rates were a little bit mixed this morning amid uncertainty over the near-term direction of the market. There was little impact from Tuesday's employment cost index and most people were sitting on the sidelines," a local dealer said.

"The market is now waiting for today's GDP, APICS, NAPM and PMI data, but the main focus will be on the GDP numbers. I don't think there will be much impact as most people are waiting for Friday's employment report and the market will be closed tomorrow for the May Day holiday," he said.
In short dates, Wednesday/Thursday rose 1/16 percentage point to 5-15/16 5-13/16 percent but Thursday/Friday eased 1/16 point to 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent.
Week-fixed was unchanged from Tuesday's 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent.
Among term rates, one-month was unchanged at 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent and three-months unchanged at 5-7/8 5-3/4 percent.
Nine-months eased 1/16 point to 6-3/16 6-1/16 percent and twelve-months eased 1/8 point to 6-5/16 6-3/16 percent.
